newsitem.title: USA: AT&T posts expected decline in operating income.
newsitem.headline: AT&T posts expected decline in operating income.

text.p: AT&T Corp., which had warned of weaker results from its core long-distance phone business, Thursday reported a fivefold jump in profits to $1.43 billion for the third quarter, although its income from continuing operations fell 11 percent.

The telecommunications giant's net income, equal to 89 cents a share, increased from $262 million, or 16 cents a share, in the year-ago period, when it took a one-time charge of $1.6 billion for its restructuring and for cost reductions at its NCR unit.
AT&T's revenues in the latest quarter were $13.2 billion, up from $12.9 billion.

The company had projected last month that its income from continuing operations would be lower in the third quarter. Operating earnings fell to $1.36 billion, or 84 cents a share, from $1.53 billion, or 96 cents a share.
AT&T said on Sept. 24 that its income from continuing operations might fall as much as 10 cents short of Wall Street analysts' expectations of income equal to 92 cents a share.
It said its operating income was hurt by competitive pressure in the long-distance telephone market, customer care enhancements and investments in local, on-line and wireless capabilities.
AT&T's stock was unchanged at $39.875 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
